## `audit.py`

Summarize, prune and rotate the ssh-core audit trail in $TMPDIR/ssh-core. Answers 'which host failed most in the last 24h' without a throwaway jq pipeline.

```text
audit.py [-h] [--json] [--version] {summarize,prune,rotate,list} ...
```

|---|---|---|
| `cmd` | yes | - |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--json` | - | - | - |
| `--version`, `-V` | - | - | - |

## `deploy_pubkey.py`

Install a public key on a remote host over SSH (no ssh-copy-id needed), verify that key-only auth works, and optionally promote the host's # auth: metadata to key.

```text
deploy_pubkey.py [-h] [--key KEY] [--connect-timeout CONNECT_TIMEOUT]
                        [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG]
                        [--accept-new-hostkey] [--password]
                        [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV] [--promote-auth]
                        [--redact] [--audit-log] [--no-audit] [--json]
                        [--version]
                        alias
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `alias` | yes | Host alias from ~/.ssh/config (or user@host) |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--key` | - | - | Path to the .pub file (default: first of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub / ~/.ssh/id_ecdsa.pub / ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub / ~/.ssh/id_dsa.pub) |
| `--connect-timeout` | 8 | - | - |
| `--timeout` | 180 | - | - |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | Pass -F <path> to ssh |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | Opt-in: StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new for first-touch trust |
| `--password` | false | - | Headless bootstrap: log in with $SSH_PASSWORD, append the key, then verify key-only auth. No TTY or ssh-copy-id needed. |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | - |
| `--promote-auth` | false | - | After a verified install: rewrite '# auth:' to key and add IdentityFile/IdentitiesOnly for this alias |
| `--redact` | true | - | Hide host identifiers in the envelope (default: on) |
| `--no-redact` | true | - | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ (default: on when SSH_CORE_AUDIT=on) |
| `--no-audit` | true | - | Do not write audit records |
| `--json` | false | - | - |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | - |

## `doctor.py`

Prove which ssh-core capabilities actually work here: local tools, a staged askpass helper, and (with --host) real connect / transfer / sudo probes. --profile full additionally probes the backends of the other seven plugins in this marketplace. Use --require to gate a deployment.

```text
doctor.py [-h] [--profile {transport,full}] [--host HOST]
                 [--hosts HOSTS] [--modes MODES] [--user USER]
                 [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG] [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV]
                 [--accept-new-hostkey] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--no-transfer]
                 [--sudo] [--require CAPABILITY] [--json] [--version]
```

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--profile` | transport | `transport`, `full` | transport (default): ssh-core's own capabilities, unchanged. full: also probe docker/podman, kubectl/helm, terraform/tofu, gh/glab, python yaml/hcl2 and journalctl/tail/nc, then print readiness per plugin and fill data.capabilities |
| `--host` | - | - | Alias, user@host or IP to probe live (implies --modes auto) |
| `--hosts` | - | - | Comma-separated targets; every probe runs against each of them |
| `--modes` | auto | - | Comma-separated auth routes to probe: auto, key, password (default: key,password — auto is expanded so a host that only accepts one of them still reports the other as broken) |
| `--user`, `-l` | - | - | Login user for the live probes (forwarded as --user) |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | Pass -F <path> to every probe |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | Environment variable holding the password (default: SSH_PASSWORD) |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | Let the probes trust an unknown host key (persisted in known_hosts) |
| `--timeout` | 30 | - | Per-probe timeout in seconds (default: 30) |
| `--no-transfer` | true | - | Skip the upload/download round trip |
| `--sudo` | false | - | Also prove `sudo -n` works on the target |
| `--require` | [] | - | Exit 9 unless this capability works; repeatable. Known names: askpass, config, exec_key, exec_password, paramiko, rsync, scp, sftp, ssh, sudo, tar, transfer. With --profile full a plugin id also works (e.g. --require k8s-debug, --require docker), gating on that plugin's readiness row. |
| `--json` | false | - | - |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | - |

## `selfcheck.py`

Report which ssh-core capabilities work on this machine, dependency-free. Exits 0 when everything required is present.

```text
selfcheck.py [-h] [--check NAME] [--strict] [--write-matrix PATH]
                    [--json] [--version]
```

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--check` | [] | - | Fail (exit 9) unless this tool/capability is usable; repeatable. Known names: paramiko, rsync, scp, sftp, ssh, ssh-copy-id, ssh-keygen, tar, transfer |
| `--strict` | false | - | Also fail when no file-transfer backend at all is available |
| `--write-matrix` | - | - | Write references/platform-matrix.md (regenerated from this probe) instead of printing the table (DV-26) |
| `--json` | false | - | - |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | - |

## `ssh_cluster.py`

Broadcast one command across a fleet. Delegates each host to ssh_execute.py via subprocess. Targets come from --hosts and/or the ~/.ssh/config metadata filters --tags / --environment (AND-combined).

```text
ssh_cluster.py [-h] [--hosts HOSTS] [--tags TAGS]
                      [--environment ENVIRONMENT] [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG]
                      [--stdin-file PATH] [--auth {auto,key,password}]
                      [--user USER] [--allow-exit CODES]
                      [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV] [--accept-new-hostkey]
                      [-o KEY=VALUE] [--parallel] [--max-workers MAX_WORKERS]
                      [--health-check] [--health-check-command CMD]
                      [--probe [tcp:|port:]PORT] [--probe-timeout SECONDS]
                      [--fail-fast] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                      [--connect-timeout CONNECT_TIMEOUT] [--json] [--version]
                      [--audit-log] [--no-audit] [--retry N]
                      [--retry-delay SECONDS] [--retry-backoff FACTOR]
                      [--redact]
                      command
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | yes | Remote command string (passed to ssh_execute) |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--hosts` | - | - | Comma-separated host aliases |
| `--tags` | - | - | Comma-separated tags; matches hosts whose '# tags:' metadata contains every tag (AND). Resolves against ~/.ssh/config. |
| `--environment` | - | - | Match hosts whose '# environment:' metadata equals this value. Resolves against ~/.ssh/config. |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | Config file used BOTH to resolve targets (--tags / --environment) and to connect: it is forwarded as ssh -F to every worker, so the host selected is the host connected to (SSHCORE-018). Default: ~/.ssh/config |
| `--stdin-file` | - | - | File piped to every worker's stdin (each host opens its own handle). Cluster never inherits the caller's stdin: with N workers sharing one fd only one host would read the data and all would report success (SSHCORE-024) |
| `--auth` | auto | `auto`, `key`, `password` | Auth routing forwarded to every host: 'auto' reads the `# auth:` metadata written by ssh_config_manager. 'password' answers OpenSSH's prompt with a temporary SSH_ASKPASS helper and reads the secret from --password-env; the command channel stays a normal exec channel (no pty, no `-tt`), so stdout/stderr stay separate and the remote exit code is real. On POSIX the same askpass route is used whether or not a pty exists (review B2: the old help text said 'via the pty session', which was wrong on Windows and only half-true on Linux) |
| `--user`, `-l` | - | - | Forward `--user USER` to every worker: password auth against a bare IP whose config block has no `User` is refused with user_required (exit 115) instead of trying the local account name (review B1) |
| `--allow-exit`, `--expect-exit` | - | - | Comma-separated exit codes that count as success on every host, e.g. `0,1` for grep/diff (review C1). Forwarded to each worker and applied to the aggregated verdict |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | Environment variable holding the password (default: SSH_PASSWORD) |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | Forward --accept-new-hostkey to every worker: an unknown host key is added to known_hosts instead of aborting. The key is *persisted*, so later calls trust it without the flag; a changed key still fails with host_key (review B3) |
| `-o`, `--ssh-option` | [] | - | Extra `ssh -o` option forwarded to every host; repeatable |
| `--parallel` | false | - | Accepted for compatibility; concurrency is governed entirely by --max-workers and passing --parallel is a no-op. |
| `--max-workers` | 8 | - | Thread pool size (default: 8). Set to 1 for deterministic serial execution. |
| `--health-check` | false | - | Probe each host before the broadcast and skip the ones that fail. The probe is `true` unless --health-check-command says otherwise, and --probe adds transport-level checks (DV-15) |
| `--health-check-command` | true | - | Command whose non-zero exit marks a host unhealthy, e.g. 'systemctl is-active nginx' (default: true, which only proves that SSH works) (DV-15) |
| `--probe` | [] | - | Also probe a TCP port without using ssh (repeatable), e.g. --probe tcp:22 --probe port:3306. Results land in data.results[alias].probe; a closed port marks the host unhealthy. |
| `--probe-timeout` | 3.0 | - | Per-probe TCP connect timeout (default: 3.0) |
| `--fail-fast` | false | - | Stop submitting new hosts after the first failure. Already-running workers complete; unstarted hosts get failure_class=skipped_fail_fast. |
| `--timeout` | 120 | - | Per-host command timeout (default: 120s) |
| `--connect-timeout` | 8 | - | SSH ConnectTimeout (default: 8s) |
| `--json` | false | - | Emit the shared JSON output contract on stdout |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | Print the ssh-core version |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ (default: on when SSH_CORE_AUDIT=on) |
| `--no-audit` | true | - | Do not write audit records |
| `--retry` | 1 | - | Total attempts for transient failures (default: 1 = no retry). Only failure_class network/timeout are repeated; auth and host-key failures never are. |
| `--retry-delay` | 2.0 | - | Wait before the second attempt (default: 2.0) |
| `--retry-backoff` | 2.0 | - | Multiplier applied to the delay after each failed attempt (default: 2.0; use 1.0 for a fixed delay) |
| `--redact` | true | - | Hide host identifiers in the envelope (default: on) |
| `--no-redact` | true | - | ==SUPPRESS== |

## `ssh_config_manager.py`

CRUD + restore over ~/.ssh/config: create / update / delete / list / find / restore / validate. Writes are locked, atomic, backed up and validated with `ssh -G` before they land.

```text
ssh_config_manager.py [-h] [--json] [--config-path CONFIG_PATH]
                             [--audit-log] [--version]
                             {create,update,delete,list,find,restore,validate}
                             ...
```

|---|---|---|
| `cmd` | yes | - |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--json` | - | - | Emit the shared JSON output contract on stdout |
| `--config-path` | - | - | Override default ~/.ssh/config (mainly for tests) |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | Print the ssh-core version |

Keep one SSH session per alias alive and run commands through it, so repeated calls cost no extra handshake (works on Windows too).

```text
ssh_daemon.py [-h] [--json] [--audit-log] [--version]
                     {start,run,status,stop,list,_serve} ...
```

| `--json` | - | - | Emit the shared JSON envelope |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | - |

## `ssh_download.py`

Copy a file or tree from a remote alias to this host. Uses SFTP when paramiko is installed and falls back to scp/tar otherwise.

```text
ssh_download.py [-h] [--transport {auto,sftp,scp,openssh}] [--resume]
                       [--recursive] [--preserve] [--delete] [--yes]
                       [--no-progress] [--bwlimit BWLIMIT]
                       [--block-size BLOCK_SIZE] [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG]
                       [--port PORT] [--identity IDENTITY]
                       [--accept-new-hostkey] [--auth {auto,key,password}]
                       [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                       [--redact] [--audit-log] [--no-audit] [--retry N]
                       [--retry-delay SECONDS] [--retry-backoff FACTOR]
                       [--json] [--version]
                       alias remote_path local_path
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `alias` | yes | - |
| `remote_path` | yes | - |
| `local_path` | yes | - |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--transport` | auto | `auto`, `sftp`, `scp`, `openssh` | Transfer backend: sftp/paramiko (resume, bwlimit, verify), or scp/openssh (the OpenSSH client itself, no paramiko needed). 'openssh' is an explicit alias for the scp backend; 'auto' picks sftp when paramiko is importable and scp otherwise (SSHCORE-026) |
| `--resume` | false | - | - |
| `--recursive` | false | - | - |
| `--preserve` | false | - | Apply the remote file's mtime and permission bits to the local copy (cp -p semantics); SFTP only, reported in data.preserved (DV-19) |
| `--delete` | false | - | MIRROR mode: remove local entries that no longer exist remotely. Destructive — requires --yes and only runs after a clean copy (DV-19) |
| `--yes`, `-y` | false | - | Confirm the destructive --delete mirror (no prompt is ever shown) |
| `--no-progress` | false | - | - |
| `--bwlimit` | - | - | - |
| `--block-size` | 131072 | - | SFTP block size in bytes (default: 131072) |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | - |
| `--port` | - | - | - |
| `--identity` | - | - | - |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | - |
| `--auth` | auto | `auto`, `key`, `password` | Authentication routing for the scp/tar backends: 'auto' reads # auth: password from --ssh-config, 'password' answers the prompt through SSH_ASKPASS. Without it a password-only host could not transfer at all without paramiko (SSHCORE-026) |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | Environment variable holding the password (default: SSH_PASSWORD) |
| `--timeout` | 1800 | - | - |
| `--redact` | true | - | Hide host identifiers in the envelope (default: on) |
| `--no-redact` | true | - | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ (default: on when SSH_CORE_AUDIT=on) |
| `--no-audit` | true | - | Do not write audit records |
| `--retry` | 1 | - | Total attempts for transient failures (default: 1 = no retry). Only failure_class network/timeout are repeated; auth and host-key failures never are. |
| `--retry-delay` | 2.0 | - | Wait before the second attempt (default: 2.0) |
| `--retry-backoff` | 2.0 | - | Multiplier applied to the delay after each failed attempt (default: 2.0; use 1.0 for a fixed delay) |
| `--json` | false | - | - |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | - |

## `ssh_execute.py`

Run a command on a remote host (or 'local'). Emits the shared JSON contract with --json. Local commands run without a shell; use `bash -c '...'` as the explicit escape hatch.

```text
ssh_execute.py [-h] [--user USER] [--command COMMANDS]
                      [--commands-file COMMANDS_FILE]
                      [--stdin-text STDIN_TEXT] [--stdin-file PATH]
                      [--script-file PATH] [--normalize-lf] [--keep-crlf]
                      [--output-file PATH] [--allow-exit CODES]
                      [--redact-host] [--no-redact-host] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                      [--connect-timeout CONNECT_TIMEOUT]
                      [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG] [--port PORT]
                      [--identity IDENTITY] [--control-master {off,auto}]
                      [--control-persist CONTROL_PERSIST]
                      [--control-path-dir CONTROL_PATH_DIR] [-o KEY=VALUE]
                      [--auth {auto,key,password}]
                      [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV] [--accept-new-hostkey]
                      [--sudo] [--sudo-user USER] [--sudo-preserve-env]
                      [--sudo-password-env VAR] [--follow] [--tail N]
                      [--redact] [--no-redact] [--audit-log] [--no-audit]
                      [--retry N] [--retry-delay SECONDS]
                      [--retry-backoff FACTOR]
                      [--shell {none,cmd,powershell,sh}] [--json] [--version]
                      host [command]
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | yes | Host alias from ~/.ssh/config, user@host, user@host:port, or the literal 'local' |
| `command` | no | Command to run on the host (argv string). Omit it when using --commands-file/--stdin-text/--script-file, or to open a login shell's stdin. Prefix with '--' when the command starts with '-'. |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--user`, `-l` | - | - | Remote login user. Without it, a bare host/IP whose config block has no `User` is rejected for password auth (failure_class=user_required, exit 115) instead of silently logging in as the local Windows account (review B1) |
| `--command` | [] | - | Command to run in a batch over ONE connection; repeatable (SSH-12: the Windows-safe replacement for ControlMaster) |
| `--commands-file` | - | - | File with one command per line ('#' comments and blanks skipped) |
| `--stdin-text` | - | - | Text piped to the remote command's stdin (single connection) |
| `--stdin-file` | - | - | File whose bytes are piped to the remote command's stdin; unlike --stdin-text the content never enters argv (or the audit log). ssh_cluster forwards this per worker (SSHCORE-024)Bytes are passed through verbatim; add --normalize-lf for a file produced by PowerShell (BOM + CRLF) (review D4) |
| `--script-file` | - | - | Run a local script ON THE REMOTE HOST as `bash -s` (the command itself is then optional). This sidesteps the three-level quoting problem entirely: write the script locally, pass it here, and never fight `$`, quotes or awk programs through pwsh -> ssh -> sh (review D3). Implies --normalize-lf unless you pass --keep-crlf |
| `--normalize-lf` | false | - | Strip a UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM and convert CRLF (and lone CR) to LF in --stdin-file / --script-file. Off by default: the transport is byte-exact, and PowerShell's Set-Content/Out-File output would otherwise reach bash as '\ufeffhostname: command not found' (review D4) |
| `--keep-crlf` | false | - | Do not normalise line endings even for --script-file (which normalises by default). Use when the payload is not a shell script |
| `--output-file` | - | - | Write the command's stdout to PATH in full, bypassing the 10 MB in-envelope cap. The envelope then carries only path/bytes/sha256/truncation flags (data.output_file) instead of the transcript. This is the answer to 'journalctl dumped 235 MB and the envelope kept 10 MB' (review D1) |
| `--allow-exit`, `--expect-exit` | - | - | Comma-separated exit codes that count as success, e.g. `0,1` for grep/diff or `0,2` for curl. A command exiting with an allowed code reports success=true, data.exit_allowed=true and keeps the real exit_code (review C1 — the single most requested flag) |
| `--redact-host` | true | - | Hide the host identity in the envelope (default). data.host_id stays available either way (review C4) |
| `--no-redact-host` | true | - | Keep the raw host string in data.host_id (still not the HostName) |
| `--timeout` | 120 | - | Total wall-clock budget in seconds (default: 120) |
| `--connect-timeout` | 8 | - | SSH connect timeout, applied as -o ConnectTimeout (default: 8) |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | Pass -F <path> to ssh (default: ~/.ssh/config) |
| `--port`, `-p` | - | - | Remote port (-p); overrides Port from the config (SSH-23) |
| `--identity`, `-i` | - | - | Private key path (-i -o IdentitiesOnly=yes) (SSH-23) |
| `--control-master` | off | `off`, `auto` | Opt into OpenSSH ControlMaster reuse (POSIX only; on Windows use --commands-file instead - SSH-12) |
| `--control-persist` | 600 | - | ControlPersist seconds when --control-master=auto (default: 600) |
| `--control-path-dir` | - | - | Directory for ControlMaster sockets (default: temp dir) |
| `-o`, `--ssh-option` | [] | - | Extra `ssh -o` option; repeatable. Example: -o KexAlgorithms=+diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1. ProxyCommand / LocalCommand / Match and friends are refused. |
| `--auth` | auto | `auto`, `key`, `password` | Auth routing: 'key' forces BatchMode publickey; 'password' uses the pty (POSIX) or SSH_ASKPASS over pipes (Windows); 'auto' reads # auth: metadata (default: auto) |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | Environment variable holding the password (default: SSH_PASSWORD) |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | Trust an as-yet-unknown host key via StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new on both the key and password routes (SSH-06). This is NOT strictly one-shot: the key is appended to known_hosts and every later call trusts it silently. A *changed* key still fails with host_key (review B3) |
| `--sudo` | false | - | Run the command under sudo, non-interactively: `sudo -n [-u USER] -- sh -c '<cmd>'`. A missing NOPASSWD rule fails fast with failure_class=sudo_required (exit 112) instead of hanging on a prompt. Pick the target user with --sudo-user USER (DV-14); `--sudo=USER` is not accepted |
| `--sudo-user` | root | - | Target user for --sudo (default: root) |
| `--sudo-preserve-env` | false | - | Pass -E to sudo so the remote command keeps its environment |
| `--sudo-password-env` | - | - | Feed the sudo password from this environment variable over stdin (`sudo -S`). Opt-in; a NOPASSWD sudoers rule is the better answer. Needs a single command (no --commands-file/--stdin-text) |
| `--follow`, `-f` | false | - | Keep streaming output until Ctrl-C or --timeout, like `tail -f`. The live transcript goes to stderr with --json and to stdout otherwise; the final envelope is still valid JSON (DV-18) |
| `--tail` | - | - | With --follow: start from the last N lines (wraps the command in `stdbuf -oL sh -c ... \| tail -n N -f`). Ignored without --follow. |
| `--redact` | true | - | Hide HostName/User/Port/IdentityFile in the envelope (default: on) |
| `--no-redact` | true | - | Debug: keep raw host identifiers in the envelope |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ (default: on when SSH_CORE_AUDIT=on) |
| `--no-audit` | true | - | Do not write audit records |
| `--retry` | 1 | - | Total attempts for transient failures (default: 1 = no retry). Only failure_class network/timeout are repeated; auth and host-key failures never are. |
| `--retry-delay` | 2.0 | - | Wait before the second attempt (default: 2.0) |
| `--retry-backoff` | 2.0 | - | Multiplier applied to the delay after each failed attempt (default: 2.0; use 1.0 for a fixed delay) |
| `--shell` | none | `none`, `cmd`, `powershell`, `sh` | Local route only: run the command through this shell instead of executing it directly. 'none' (default) keeps the no-shell rule and the metacharacter refusal. 'cmd' / 'powershell' (Windows) and 'sh' (POSIX) are the declared form of the escape hatch, e.g. `local --shell cmd "echo hello"`; the inline forms `cmd /c ...` and `powershell -Command ...` keep working and stay subject to the metacharacter refusal (GAP-008) |
| `--json` | false | - | Emit the shared JSON output contract on stdout |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | Print the ssh-core version |

## `ssh_server_transfer.py`

Move bytes between two remote hosts. stream = SFTP through this host (needs paramiko); direct = tar/rsync between the two hosts (no paramiko); auto picks stream when paramiko is available.

```text
ssh_server_transfer.py [-h] [--mode {auto,direct,stream,hybrid}]
                              [--use-rsync] [--recursive] [--bwlimit BWLIMIT]
                              [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG] [--accept-new-hostkey]
                              [--auth {auto,key,password}]
                              [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV]
                              [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--redact] [--audit-log]
                              [--no-audit] [--json] [--version]
                              src_alias src_path dst_alias dst_path
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `src_alias` | yes | - |
| `src_path` | yes | - |
| `dst_alias` | yes | - |
| `dst_path` | yes | - |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--mode` | auto | `auto`, `direct`, `stream`, `hybrid` | Transfer mode (default: auto) |
| `--use-rsync` | false | - | Use rsync for the direct path (incremental). rsync must be installed on the SOURCE host: both endpoints are remote, so it cannot run from this machine |
| `--recursive` | false | - | - |
| `--bwlimit` | - | - | KB/s cap (1 KB = 1024 B/s) |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | - |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | - |
| `--auth` | auto | `auto`, `key`, `password` | Authentication routing for the direct (tar/rsync) backends: 'auto' reads '# auth: password' metadata for BOTH aliases, 'password' answers the prompt through SSH_ASKPASS. Without it a password-only host could not copy server-to-server (SSHCORE-026) |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | Environment variable holding the password (default: SSH_PASSWORD) |
| `--timeout` | 1800 | - | - |
| `--redact` | true | - | Hide host identifiers in the envelope (default: on) |
| `--no-redact` | true | - | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ (default: on when SSH_CORE_AUDIT=on) |
| `--no-audit` | true | - | Do not write audit records |
| `--json` | false | - | - |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | - |

## `ssh_session.py`

Interactive SSH session for password-only hosts and network-device CLIs. Password comes from $SSH_PASSWORD (or --password-env); it is never placed in argv. Uses a real pty on POSIX and `ssh -tt` + SSH_ASKPASS elsewhere.

```text
ssh_session.py [-h] [--user USER] [--command COMMANDS]
                      [--command-file COMMAND_FILE]
                      [--disable-paging DISABLE_PAGING]
                      [--prompt-regex PROMPT_REGEX] [--no-capture-output]
                      [--confirm {ask,yes,no}]
                      [--connect-timeout CONNECT_TIMEOUT] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                      [--step-timeout STEP_TIMEOUT] [--force-pty] [--no-pty]
                      [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG] [-o KEY=VALUE]
                      [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV] [--accept-new-hostkey]
                      [--audit-log] [--no-audit] [--snapshot-cmd SNAPSHOT_CMD]
                      [--snapshot-dir SNAPSHOT_DIR] [--json] [--version]
                      host
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | yes | Host alias from ~/.ssh/config (or user@host) |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--user`, `-l` | - | - | Login user, forwarded as `ssh -l USER`. A network device reached by bare IP has no `user@` and often no `User` block, which is exactly when ssh picks the local account name and the login fails with a misleading 'Permission denied' (review B1) |
| `--command` | [] | - | Command to send, in order; repeatable |
| `--command-file` | - | - | File with one command per line ('#' comments and blanks skipped) |
| `--disable-paging` | - | - | Sent first, e.g. "screen-length 0 temporary" (VRP) or "terminal length 0" (IOS) |
| `--prompt-regex` | - | - | Regex for the device prompt (default: heuristic <...> / [...] / word>$#%%) |
| `--no-capture-output` | false | - | Only report output_bytes per command instead of the transcript (smaller envelopes; the default returns data.results[].output) |
| `--confirm` | ask | `ask`, `yes`, `no` | How to answer [Y/N] prompts (default: ask → fail with confirmation_required so the user opts in explicitly) |
| `--connect-timeout` | 8 | - | SSH ConnectTimeout in seconds (default: 8) |
| `--timeout` | 180 | - | Whole-session budget in seconds (default: 180) |
| `--step-timeout` | 30 | - | Per-command prompt wait in seconds (default: 30) |
| `--force-pty` | - | - | Require a POSIX pty (fails on Windows instead of using pipes) |
| `--no-pty` | - | - | Use `ssh -tt` + SSH_ASKPASS even on POSIX |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | Pass -F <path> to ssh |
| `-o`, `--ssh-option` | [] | - | Extra `ssh -o` option; repeatable |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | Environment variable holding the password (default: SSH_PASSWORD) |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | Opt-in: StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new for first-touch trust |
| `--audit-log` | true | - | Append a JSONL audit record per command (default: on) |
| `--no-audit` | true | - | Disable the audit log |
| `--snapshot-cmd` | - | - | Capture this command's output before and after the session |
| `--snapshot-dir` | - | - | Where snapshots go (default: $TMPDIR/ssh-core/<md5(alias)>/) |
| `--json` | false | - | Emit the shared JSON contract |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | Print the ssh-core version |

## `ssh_slice.py`

Read a bounded slice of a remote file with an explicit range and a resumable cursor. No hand-written sed/grep, no quoting to escape, no 10 MB surprise: the body comes back in data.content (and stdout) and data.range.next_offset resumes it.

```text
ssh_slice.py [-h] [--stat] [--head N] [--tail N] [--lines A-B]
                    [--bytes A-B] [--grep PATTERN] [--context N]
                    [--max-bytes MAX_BYTES] [--max-lines MAX_LINES]
                    [--next-offset] [--output-file PATH] [--append]
                    [--auth {auto,key,password}] [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV]
                    [--user USER] [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG]
                    [--accept-new-hostkey] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [-o KEY=VALUE]
                    [--no-redact] [--json] [--version]
                    host remote_path
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | yes | Alias from ~/.ssh/config, user@host or an IP |
| `remote_path` | yes | Absolute path on the remote host |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--stat` | false | - | Report line and byte counts instead of content |
| `--head` | - | - | First N lines |
| `--tail` | - | - | Last N lines (bounded by --max-bytes) |
| `--lines` | - | - | Line range, 1-based and inclusive (e.g. 299700-302600) |
| `--bytes` | - | - | Byte range, 0-based and inclusive |
| `--grep` | - | - | Extended regex, matched with `grep -n -E`; output keeps line numbers so a hit can be turned into --lines |
| `--context` | 0 | - | With --grep: N lines of context (grep -B/-A) |
| `--max-bytes` | 4194304 | - | Cap on the returned slice (default 4194304, max 67108864) |
| `--max-lines` | 200000 | - | Cap on returned lines (default 200000) |
| `--next-offset` | false | - | Include data.range.next_offset (always on; kept as a readable flag for scripts that want to be explicit) |
| `--output-file` | - | - | Also write the slice to this local file (append with --append for a resumable download) |
| `--append` | false | - | With --output-file: append instead of overwrite, so a loop over next_offset reconstructs the whole file |
| `--auth` | auto | `auto`, `key`, `password` | Forwarded to ssh_execute (default: auto) |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | Environment variable holding the password |
| `--user`, `-l` | - | - | Login user |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | Pass -F <path> to ssh |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | Trust an unknown host key (persisted in known_hosts) |
| `--timeout` | 120 | - | Timeout for the remote read (default: 120) |
| `-o`, `--ssh-option` | [] | - | Extra `ssh -o` option; repeatable |
| `--no-redact` | false | - | Debug: keep raw host identifiers in the envelope |
| `--json` | false | - | - |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | - |

## `ssh_tunnel.py`

Manage SSH port forwards (-L local, -R remote, -D SOCKS) as detached processes with a state file, an optional idle watchdog and audit records.

```text
ssh_tunnel.py [-h] [--json] [--audit-log] [--no-audit] [--version]
                     {start,stop,status,list,_watch} ...
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `cmd` | yes | - |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--json` | - | - | Emit the JSON envelope |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ |
| `--no-audit` | - | - | Do not write audit records |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | Print version |

## `ssh_upload.py`

Copy a file or tree from this host to a remote alias. Uses SFTP when paramiko is installed and falls back to scp otherwise.

```text
ssh_upload.py [-h] [--transport {auto,sftp,scp,openssh}] [--resume]
                     [--recursive] [--overwrite] [--preserve] [--delete]
                     [--yes] [--no-progress] [--chmod CHMOD]
                     [--bwlimit BWLIMIT] [--block-size BLOCK_SIZE]
                     [--ssh-config SSH_CONFIG] [--port PORT]
                     [--identity IDENTITY] [--accept-new-hostkey]
                     [--auth {auto,key,password}]
                     [--password-env PASSWORD_ENV] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                     [--redact] [--audit-log] [--no-audit] [--retry N]
                     [--retry-delay SECONDS] [--retry-backoff FACTOR] [--json]
                     [--version]
                     alias local_path remote_path
```

| Positional | Required | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `alias` | yes | - |
| `local_path` | yes | - |
| `remote_path` | yes | - |

| Option | Default | Choices | Help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | show this help message and exit |
| `--transport` | auto | `auto`, `sftp`, `scp`, `openssh` | Transfer backend: sftp/paramiko (resume, chmod, bwlimit, verify), or scp/openssh (the OpenSSH client itself, no paramiko needed). 'openssh' is an explicit alias for the scp backend; 'auto' picks sftp when paramiko is importable and scp otherwise (SSHCORE-026) |
| `--resume` | false | - | Resume a partial SFTP transfer |
| `--recursive` | false | - | - |
| `--overwrite` | false | - | Replace the remote file if it already exists. Without this flag an existing destination is refused with failure_class=remote_path_exists (exit 168) and left untouched (GAP-003). --resume and --delete (mirror) imply it, because both of them are defined as writing over what is already there. Recursive uploads land *inside* the remote directory, so an existing directory target is normal and is never refused |
| `--preserve` | false | - | Copy mtime and permission bits as well as content (cp -p semantics); SFTP only, reported in data.preserved (DV-19) |
| `--delete` | false | - | MIRROR mode: remove remote entries that do not exist locally. Destructive — requires --yes and only runs after a clean copy (DV-19) |
| `--yes`, `-y` | false | - | Confirm the destructive --delete mirror (no prompt is ever shown) |
| `--no-progress` | false | - | - |
| `--chmod` | - | - | Octal mode for the remote file (SFTP) |
| `--bwlimit` | - | - | Bandwidth cap in KB/s |
| `--block-size` | 131072 | - | SFTP block size in bytes (default: 131072) |
| `--ssh-config` | - | - | Read host/IdentityFile from this file |
| `--port` | - | - | Remote port override |
| `--identity` | - | - | Private key path override |
| `--accept-new-hostkey` | false | - | Trust an unknown host key once (accept-new) |
| `--auth` | auto | `auto`, `key`, `password` | Authentication routing for the scp backend: 'auto' reads # auth: password from --ssh-config, 'password' answers the prompt through SSH_ASKPASS. Without it a password-only host could not transfer at all without paramiko (SSHCORE-026) |
| `--password-env` | SSH_PASSWORD | - | Environment variable holding the password (default: SSH_PASSWORD) |
| `--timeout` | 1800 | - | Transfer timeout in seconds (default: 1800) |
| `--redact` | true | - | Hide host identifiers in the envelope (default: on) |
| `--no-redact` | true | - | ==SUPPRESS== |
| `--audit-log` | - | - | Append a JSONL audit record under $TMPDIR/ssh-core/ (default: on when SSH_CORE_AUDIT=on) |
| `--no-audit` | true | - | Do not write audit records |
| `--retry` | 1 | - | Total attempts for transient failures (default: 1 = no retry). Only failure_class network/timeout are repeated; auth and host-key failures never are. |
| `--retry-delay` | 2.0 | - | Wait before the second attempt (default: 2.0) |
| `--retry-backoff` | 2.0 | - | Multiplier applied to the delay after each failed attempt (default: 2.0; use 1.0 for a fixed delay) |
| `--json` | false | - | - |
| `--version`, `-V` | false | - | Print the ssh-core version |

## Exit codes

`EXIT_CODES` is the only failure_class -> exit_code mapping. A
script must call `exit_code_for()` instead of hardcoding a number.
`255` is OpenSSH's own client-failure code and is passed through
unchanged; it is not part of this table.

| Code | failure_class | Constant |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `ok` | `EXIT_OK` |
| 1 | `all_hosts_failed`, `internal`, `partial_failure`, `skipped_fail_fast`, `ssh_execute_broken` | `EXIT_INTERNAL` |
| 2 | `invalid_arguments` | `EXIT_INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 3 | `dependency_missing`, `ssh_execute_missing` | `EXIT_DEPENDENCY_MISSING` |
| 4 | `alias_not_found`, `not_found`, `target_resolution_failed` | `EXIT_NOT_FOUND` |
| 5 | `already_exists` | `EXIT_ALREADY_EXISTS` |
| 6 | `config_missing` | `EXIT_CONFIG_MISSING` |
| 7 | `parse_error` | `EXIT_PARSE_ERROR` |
| 8 | `permission` | `EXIT_PERMISSION` |
| 9 | `transfer_verify_failed`, `verify_failed` | `EXIT_VERIFY_FAILED` |
| 100 | `auth`, `auth_dst`, `auth_src` | `EXIT_AUTH` |
| 101 | `host_key` | `EXIT_HOST_KEY` |
| 102 | `health_check_failed`, `network`, `network_dst`, `network_src` | `EXIT_NETWORK` |
| 103 | `kex` | `EXIT_KEX` |
| 104 | `remote_error` | `EXIT_REMOTE_ERROR` |
| 105 | `password_required` | `EXIT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED` |
| 106 | `no_tty_for_password` | `EXIT_NO_TTY` |
| 107 | `invalid_option` | `EXIT_INVALID_OPTION` |
| 108 | `unsupported_target` | `EXIT_UNSUPPORTED_TARGET` |
| 109 | `confirmation_required` | `EXIT_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` |
| 110 | `prompt_timeout` | `EXIT_PROMPT_TIMEOUT` |
| 112 | `sudo_required` | `EXIT_SUDO_REQUIRED` |
| 113 | `sudo_auth_failed` | `EXIT_SUDO_AUTH_FAILED` |
| 114 | `askpass_unavailable` | `EXIT_ASKPASS_UNAVAILABLE` |
| 115 | `user_required` | `EXIT_USER_REQUIRED` |
| 120 | `posix_only` | `EXIT_POSIX_ONLY` |
| 121 | `port_busy` | `EXIT_PORT_BUSY` |
| 122 | `port_pool_exhausted` | `EXIT_PORT_POOL_EXHAUSTED` |
| 123 | `ssh_connect_failed` | `EXIT_SSH_CONNECT_FAILED` |
| 124 | `timeout` | `EXIT_TIMEOUT` |
| 125 | `forward_setup_failed` | `EXIT_FORWARD_SETUP_FAILED` |
| 126 | `tunnel_not_found` | `EXIT_TUNNEL_NOT_FOUND` |
| 127 | `ambiguous_stop` | `EXIT_AMBIGUOUS_STOP` |
| 128 | `stale_state_only` | `EXIT_STALE_STATE_ONLY` |
| 129 | `kill_failed` | `EXIT_KILL_FAILED` |
| 140 | `tool_missing` | `EXIT_TOOL_MISSING` |
| 141 | `key_file_missing` | `EXIT_KEY_FILE_MISSING` |
| 142 | `ssh_config_unsupported` | `EXIT_SSH_CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED` |
| 160 | `local_path_missing` | `EXIT_LOCAL_PATH_MISSING` |
| 161 | `local_path_is_directory` | `EXIT_LOCAL_PATH_IS_DIRECTORY` |
| 162 | `remote_path_missing`, `src_is_directory`, `src_path_missing` | `EXIT_REMOTE_PATH_MISSING` |
| 163 | `dst_path_invalid`, `remote_path_invalid` | `EXIT_REMOTE_PATH_INVALID` |
| 164 | `transfer_io` | `EXIT_TRANSFER_IO` |
| 165 | `integrity_mismatch` | `EXIT_TRANSFER_INTEGRITY` |
| 166 | `mode_deferred` | `EXIT_MODE_UNSUPPORTED` |
| 168 | `remote_path_exists` | `EXIT_REMOTE_PATH_EXISTS` |
| 180 | `wildcard_refused` | `EXIT_WILDCARD_REFUSED` |
| 181 | `ambiguous_alias` | `EXIT_AMBIGUOUS_ALIAS` |
| 200 | `daemon_not_running` | `EXIT_DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING` |
| 202 | `daemon_protocol` | `EXIT_DAEMON_PROTOCOL` |
| 220 | `audit_no_records` | `EXIT_AUDIT_NO_RECORDS` |
| 221 | `audit_bad_since` | `EXIT_AUDIT_BAD_SINCE` |

## Failure-class aliases

Aliases share a code because a script had already shipped that
spelling. New code must use the canonical class.

| Alias | Canonical class |
|---|---|
| `alias_not_found` | `not_found` |
| `all_hosts_failed` | `internal` |
| `auth_dst` | `auth` |
| `auth_src` | `auth` |
| `dst_path_invalid` | `remote_path_invalid` |
| `health_check_failed` | `network` |
| `network_dst` | `network` |
| `network_src` | `network` |
| `partial_failure` | `internal` |
| `skipped_fail_fast` | `internal` |
| `src_is_directory` | `remote_path_missing` |
| `src_path_missing` | `remote_path_missing` |
| `ssh_execute_broken` | `internal` |
| `ssh_execute_missing` | `dependency_missing` |
| `target_resolution_failed` | `not_found` |
| `transfer_verify_failed` | `verify_failed` |
